name: Mission Statement
purpose: Defines the organization's fundamental reason for existing and what it does for whom.
example: "To organize the world's information and make it universally accessible and useful" (Google) or "Partnering to deliver secure, reliable technology solutions" (public agency)

academicSource.title: Harvard Business School - Purposes and Functions of a Mission Statement
academicSource.description: HBS background note by Renato Tagiuri defining mission as 'a statement of why the organization exists, at the most meaningful level'

realExample.description: Comprehensive collection of mission statements from all Fortune 500 companies with analysis

additionalResource.title: Harvard Kennedy School - Strategic Planning Brief
additionalResource.description: Defines mission statements in context of strategic planning frameworks

name: Vision Statement
purpose: Describes the aspirational future state the organization seeks to achieve.
example: "A computer on every desk and in every home" (Microsoft, 1980s) or "An equitable, sustainable future where all residents thrive"

academicSource.title: Stanford Graduate School of Business - Organizational Vision Working Paper
academicSource.description: Research-based framework for setting organizational vision, enriched by study of 20 visionary companies

realExample.title: Stanford University Vision Planning Process
realExample.description: Stanford's institutional vision development with 37 white papers and conceptual framework

name: Core Values / Guiding Principles
purpose: Articulates behavioral principles and cultural norms that guide daily decisions and actions.
example: "Integrity, Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence" or Amazon's Leadership Principles

academicSource.title: MIT Sloan Management Review - Organizational Culture & Values
academicSource.description: Research on how core values align with organizational culture and behavior

realExample.title: Amazon Leadership Principles
realExample.description: 16 leadership principles that guide decision-making at Amazon

additionalResource.title: NCBI Bookshelf - Organizational Culture
additionalResource.description: Academic definition: system of shared assumptions, values, and beliefs guiding behavior

name: Purpose Statement
purpose: Sits between mission and values; defines "why we exist" in a single sentence.
example: "We serve Minnesotans by enabling secure digital government"

academicSource.title: Cesar Ritz Colleges - Simon Sinek's Golden Circle Framework
academicSource.description: Educational analysis of the 'Start with Why' purpose-driven framework

realExample.description: 170 purpose statements from Fortune 500 companies with examples from AbbVie, Adobe, Amazon, AMD

additionalResource.description: Original framework: 'People don't buy WHAT you do, they buy WHY you do it'

name: Strategic Goals
purpose: Major objectives aligned with the organization's vision, typically 3-7 long-term goals spanning 3-5 years.
example: "Achieve carbon neutrality by 2030" or "Expand into 5 new markets"

academicSource.title: University of Florida IFAS - Developing SMART Goals
academicSource.description: Process for setting goals that are Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Realistic, and Timely

name: Strategic Priorities
purpose: Current focus areas that organize work and resource allocation, often annual or biennial.

academicSource.title: Brandon University - Strategic Action Plans & Alignment Guide
academicSource.description: Cascade effect where strategy drives vision, values, priorities through organizational levels

name: Guiding Principles / Decision-Making Principles
purpose: Frameworks that help choose between competing options.
example: "Customer-first in all decisions" or "Prefer build over buy when core competency"

academicSource.description: Study of European telecom firm: guiding principles as knowledge structures with emotional content used heuristically

name: Strategic Plan
purpose: Comprehensive document integrating mission, vision, goals, strategies, and resource allocation over 3-5 years.
example: Federal agency 4-year strategic plan, corporate strategic plan

name: Annual Operating Plan (AOP)
purpose: One-year plan operationalizing strategic priorities into budgets and deliverables.
example: Corporate AOP, nonprofit annual work plan, agency plan-of-work

name: North Star Metric
purpose: Single, high-level measure that reflects the organization's ultimate value.
example: "Time to delivery for public services" or "Households lifted out of homelessness"
